question: Does scholarship-signal collateral rise as removal categories descend the classifier-confidence gradient (spam -> out-of-scope -> uncategorized)? Same rubric v2 and indicators as ZD-A1 for comparability.

method.note_structure_finding: Exactly two categories are account-stratum: spam (68.0% "User was blocked") and out-of-scope (99.2%). All other categories: 0% — record-level moderation. Take-down rows carry well-formed 10.5281/zenodo DOIs in only 97 of 18,351 cases.
method.metadata_source: OpenAlex works API incl. is_retracted flag

retraction_corroboration.finding: The retraction signal does not propagate: OpenAIRE renders retracted records as silent absence; OpenAlex retains them as unflagged live scholarship. The public warning that retraction exists to provide is destroyed in both directions.

findings: Classifier-tier gradient confirmed: scholarship-signal collateral rises tenfold from spam (1.0%) to out-of-scope (10.0%), and further to empty-reason (24.0%). Collateral concentrates in exactly the two account-stratum categories plus the uncategorized residue.

Out-of-scope is the habitat of nonstandard scholarship: sampled collateral includes ORCID-bearing psychology/neuroscience documents, multilingual reference series, and AI-native serial work — the genre-class of machine-mediated scholarship, adjudicated at account stratum and erased without trace.
Retraction propagation is 0/25: the one removal class whose purpose is public warning propagates as silent absence in one graph and unflagged presence in another.
Category corroborations where the shadow supports the label: test-record 0% scholarship-signal / 82.5% no-metadata; duplicate dominated by no-metadata (consistent with merge).
